newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open firmer, eye on two-year auction.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open firmer, eye on two-year auction.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened slightly firmer in quiet trade on Wednesday, mirroring gains in U.S. Treasuries, with much of the market focused on the results of today's auction of two-year bonds, analysts said.

"There's nothing going on. We have no news and the market is doing nothing," said Robert Marcus, vice-president of fixed-income with Altamira Investment Services. "We would expect the morning to be quiet and maybe pick up a bit in the afternoon after the auction."
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$0.17 to C$114.65 to yield 6.843 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 7/32 to yield 6.82 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to two basis points from an all-time low of one basis point at Tuesday's close.

The Government of Canada this afternoon will auction C$3.5 billion of bonds with an unspecified coupon and maturing on September 15, 1999. The Bank of Canada will buy at least C$350 million of the new bonds.
Auction results will be released at 1315 EDT/1715 GMT. The proceeds of the auction will be used for general government purposes, as there are no marketable bonds maturing on June 16.

In the interim, analysts said there was little news or significant data for the Canadian market to trade on. Instead investors were looking ahead to the release of U.S. retail sales and producer price reports on Thursday and Friday.
Beyond that, traders were focused on the July 1 meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Open Market Committee.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.17 to C$106.66 to yield 6.337 percent, while the U.S. 10-year rose 5/32 to 6.55 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 21 basis points, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.91 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 4.99 percent.
